title: Section 353 — Statements conducing to public mischief

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
353.. (1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means—
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against the public tranquillity; or
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit any offence against any other class or community,
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
(3) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine

sections.heading: Essential ingredients
sections.body:

(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit any offence against any other class or community,
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
(3) Whoever commits an offence specified in subsection (2) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine

sections.heading: Exceptions and provisos
sections.body: Exception.—It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumour or report, has reasonable grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid

Introduction. BNS s. 353 deals with Statements conducing to public mischief. It sits in Chapter XIX — Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult, Annoyance, Defamation, etc. of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Statements conducing to public mischief (old 505). Making, publishing or circulating a statement, rumour or report with intent to cause (or which is likely to cause) public alarm, mutiny, or an offence against the State or against public tranquillity — including by electronic means.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 353 is the rule on “Statements conducing to public mischief”. The section provides that . An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

2. (a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or

6. (2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
7. (3) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 353 constitutes a key component of Chapter XIX (Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult, Annoyance, Defamation, etc., and Repeal) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing statements conducing to public mischief. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of statements conducing to public mischief under Section 353 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 353.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 353 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 353 vs General Attempt: Section 353 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XIX; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 353 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 353 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult, Annoyance, Defamation, etc., and Repeal.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 353 for conduct relating to statements conducing to public mischief.
Rule: Under BNS s. 353, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 353.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 353 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
